2026-11-10.q: Which statement best captures the main point of the passage?
opts: The GRA has called a full strike for the week of the EU meetings.
Garda Commissioner Justin Kelly has resigned after talks with the GRA broke down.
The GRA has called off a planned work-to-rule after progress in talks, just before Dublin hosts major international meetings, although some wider issues remain unresolved.
The European Political Community meeting has been moved out of Dublin because of police shortages.
2026-11-10.exp: The passage says the GRA "has rescinded a proposed five-day work-to-rule shortly before Dublin hosts a series of exceptionally high-profile international meetings" owing to "considerable progress in negotiations", while "a number of broader concerns remain contingent upon the findings of the Rosters Review Group". No full strike (A), resignation (B) or relocation (D) is mentioned.

opts: They were a key concession that helped persuade the GRA to call off its action.
They were rejected by the GRA's national executive.
They will apply to every shift for the rest of the EU Presidency.
They settled all of the association's grievances permanently.

2026-11-10.q: Why does the writer mention the roughly 50 heads of government and the informal EU summit?
opts: To criticise the Government for hosting too many events at once.
To show how serious the consequences of the work-to-rule could have been.
To explain why the GRA's president was overburdened.
To suggest that the protests had been cancelled.

2026-11-10-2.q: What is the passage mainly about?
opts: Google has paid a €403 million fine and changed its location features.
The DPC has withdrawn its findings against Google after a court hearing.
The EU is drafting a new law on location data.
Google is challenging a €403 million DPC fine over location data in the High Court, including the constitutional validity of parts of Irish data law.
2026-11-10-2.exp: Google "has initiated High Court proceedings to contest a €403 million penalty" relating to "users' location data" and "intends to challenge the constitutional validity of certain provisions of the Data Protection Act 2018". It has not paid or complied (A), and the DPC has not withdrawn anything (B).

2026-11-10-2.q: What can be inferred from the fact that the case was admitted to the fast-track list "with the regulator's consent"?
opts: The DPC has accepted that its decision contained errors.
The DPC does not object to the dispute being decided relatively quickly.
The DPC will no longer require Google to comply within six months.
Google and the DPC have reached a settlement.
2026-11-10-2.exp: Consenting to the "Commercial Court's fast-track list" means the regulator was content for the case to be handled speedily. It does not mean the DPC admits errors (A) or has dropped its demands (C), and the case was "adjourned", not settled (D).

2026-11-10-2.q: How would you describe the writer's tone in the passage?
opts: Neutral and factual, reporting both the regulator's findings and Google's arguments.
Openly hostile to Google.
Enthusiastic about the fine.
Sarcastic about the Data Protection Commission.
2026-11-10-2.exp: The writer reports that the DPC "determined that location data had been combined... in the absence of a lawful basis" and that Google is "maintaining that it contains significant errors of both law and fact" without taking sides, ending with a measured note that the outcome "may have substantial implications".

opts: Dromoland Castle has closed permanently and its staff have lost their jobs.
Dromoland Castle is being sold to the owners of Adare Manor.
Dromoland Castle has closed for a €55 million six-month refurbishment, during which all permanent staff will continue to be paid.

The refurbishment was ordered by Clare County Council.

opts: To argue that the hotel's prices are too high.
To show that the company is in a strong financial position to fund the investment and keep paying staff.

To compare Dromoland with the Rine Hotel.

No prices (A), warnings (C) or comparison (D) appear.
